evidence.t: Deer here are black tailed deer, the coast form of mule deer: the synopsis calls them "mule (black-tailed) deer" (99%, Rule Book: Region 2 Lower Mainland).
Mule deer winter range u-2-005 unit G85-17-RE (official), 140 m N. Counts from October.
Cutblock harvested 2006 (20 years old), right here.
Habitat zone Coastal Western Hemlock (CWHds1): coast forest, where black tailed deer are among the most common large mammals (95%) and use logged ground often (80%) (lesson: Wet forests).
S facing slope, 17 degrees: sun melts snow first.
Private fields 1.8 km NW: deer feed on field edges (fields are private).
Black bear: young cutblocks and burns grow berries in late summer and fall (Tip).

flags.t: Route touches city limits: District of Squamish. Local firearm bylaw applies.

plan: Drive: from District of Squamish, about 10 km (straight line times 1.3, estimate). Via Squamish Valley Rd, Hwy 99.
Park: 49.85044, -123.1476, where the truck road ends (Swift Creek FSR); unload the ATV (all terrain vehicle). Map links below.
Ride: 4.2 km on unnamed roads and trails by ATV (all terrain vehicle) or 4x4 on rough road, estimate. Then walk 160 m N, climb about 5 m.
Hunt: deer, Sept, Oct, Nov, Dec (season rows). Watch the edge of the 2006 cutblock (right here) at first and last light. Sit above it with the wind in your face and glass (Tip).
Use: your .308 Winchester with a 150 to 165 grain expanding bullet (Tip).
Legal: MU (Management Unit) 2-7, Region 2. Season rows below. Study aid only. The official regulations are the law.
Verify: Candidate, scout it first. Check posted signs. Private land can be unsigned. Data dates: roads 2026-10-16, private land 2026-10-09, closures 2026-10-16.
R2B-deer-atv-0004.popWhy: Popular (more hunters): MU 2-7: about 310 hunter days a year for mule deer and white tailed deer (2020 to 2024 mean), 0.31 days per square km, middle third of BC MUs; access: close to pavement, a town or a rec site. Estimate, about 50% sure (my pick).

tags.label: Good for 2
tags.why: Cover edge here (cutblock or burn): one hunter sits at a crossing or glasses, the other walks the edge slowly with the wind at their back toward the stander. Agree zones of fire, a meeting point and a time at the truck (Tip, lesson: Hunting with a partner). Pushes are on foot only (99%, synopsis page 11, item 25).

tags.label: Good solo
tags.why: Short pack out: 0.2 km and about 5 m of climb from the parking (Tip). Cell coverage is not in the data: leave a trip plan and carry SOS or a satellite messenger (lesson: Bush safety).
